_comment: Copy to netwatch.config.json (shared) or netwatch.<hostname>.json (per host).
Only name the keys you are changing; everything else falls through to the layer below.
Unknown keys are reported at boot and ignored, so a typo cannot silently do nothing.
Relative paths resolve next to main.py (or the frozen exe); absolute paths are used verbatim.
python -c "from scapy.arch.windows import get_windows_if_list; [print(i['name'],'|',i['description']) for i in get_windows_if_list()]"
_comment_ipv6: The ISP delegates a globally-routable prefix to your LAN, so nothing structural
marks those addresses as local. Auto-detection derives the /64 from this host's
own global address; pin it explicitly (and set LOCAL_PREFIXES6_AUTO false) if the
delegation is stable and you do not want it re-derived on every boot.

_comment_retention: Packet events are compacted into one-second directional flow summaries before SQLite; packet_count preserves event totals.
_comment_capture: Events ship to the analytics core in batches; a larger batch trades a little latency for a lot less IPC overhead.
_comment_shards: Analytics shard processes (by LAN device) plus one merge process for global detectors; 1 runs the single analytics core.
_comment_detectors: Windows are divided into DETECTOR_BUCKETS sub-buckets; resolution is window/buckets and memory is O(buckets), not O(threshold).
_comment_flow: Stateful bidirectional flow records and low-jitter outbound beacon detection.
_comment_accepted_egress: ACCEPTED_EGRESS: [{macs, domains and/or cidrs, note, review_by YYYY-MM-DD}] downgrades egress-country, threat-intel and beacon findings for exactly those source MACs to an Acknowledged info case (ACCEPTED_EGRESS); past review_by it stops applying and one info case (ACCEPTED_EGRESS_EXPIRED) says so.
_comment_dns_suppressions: Use suffix suppressions for known local service-discovery zones; detections outside them remain active.
_comment_arp_confirmation: An alternate ARP owner must repeat across time before replacing a trusted binding. Quarantine sink-MAC claims are always suppressed.
_comment_policy: The policy engine dispatches block intents to the live response plane. RESPONSE_MODE decides whether they are ignored, queued, or enforced. Rules live in policy_rules.json.
_comment_evidence: A bounded in-memory raw-frame ring writes pre/post-event PCAPs only when a configured alert action fires.
_comment_suricata: Optional local EVE JSON tail; point this at a Suricata sensor output when installed.
_comment_exposure: CIDRs NetWatch owns, for a later active exposure scan. Validated at startup; nothing scans yet.
_comment_response_mode: ids_only is the fresh-install default and suppresses new containment. ready queues eligible containment for approval. autonomous immediately enforces new eligible findings. The top-right selector persists changes.
_comment_mitigation: Firewall-block a bad EXTERNAL IP on this host. The engine is live and approval-gated in ready mode. See SECURITY.md.
_comment_quarantine: Sever a LOCAL device via ARP poisoning from this host — the enforcement point
that works behind a locked ISP gateway. This EMITS forged ARP frames when an
operator approves a ready-mode action or autonomous mode selects the response.
IDS-only leaves the watcher initialized but suppresses new containment actions.

_comment_protected_pins: Never a response-action target. Empty OWN_IP is auto-detected from the default route; set it when that is not the protected address (mirror-port sensor). Empty MACs are not checked.
_comment_capture_topology: endpoint is explicitly partial. Use mirror, bridge, or gateway only when the selected capture interface actually sees whole-LAN routed traffic.
_comment_capture_coverage: Sensor health reports process and packet-loss state. Coverage is separate: complete must be an explicit, validated assertion; use partial when known traffic paths bypass this sensor.
_comment_secure_nodes: Named IP and MAC identities exposed as separate HIDE SECURE SOURCES and HIDE SECURE ENDPOINTS filters. Put host-specific values in netwatch.<hostname>.json.
